results.details: Swarm mode is not active.
results.remediation: Run: docker swarm leave --force
results.title: Ensure swarm mode is not enabled, if not needed

results.details: All containers have an AppArmor profile assigned.
results.remediation: Add --security-opt apparmor=<profile> when starting containers, or set a default AppArmor profile in /etc/docker/daemon.json.
results.title: Ensure that, if applicable, an AppArmor Profile is enabled

results.details: SELinux is not active on this host (getenforce: Disabled).
results.remediation: Use --security-opt label=type:<type> when starting containers, or ensure SELinux is Enforcing on the host and Docker is configured to use it.
results.title: Ensure that, if applicable, SELinux security options are set

results.details: All containers have acceptable capability configurations.
results.remediation: Drop all capabilities and add back only what is needed: docker run --cap-drop=ALL --cap-add=<NEEDED_CAP> ... At minimum ensure NET_RAW is dropped if not required.
results.title: Ensure that Linux kernel capabilities are restricted within containers

results.details: No privileged containers detected. All containers return Privileged=false.
results.remediation: Remove the --privileged flag from docker run commands. Use specific --cap-add flags for the exact capabilities needed instead.
results.title: Ensure that privileged containers are not used

results.details: No sensitive mounts detected.
results.remediation: Remove mounts of sensitive host directories (/, /etc, /proc, /sys, /dev etc.). Where mounts are needed, use read-only mode: -v /host/path:/container/path:ro
results.title: Ensure sensitive host system directories are not mounted on containers

results.details: No sshd process found in any running container.
results.raw_output: OCI runtime exec failed: exec failed: unable to start container process: exec: "ps": executable file not found in $PATH
results.remediation: Remove sshd from container images. Use docker exec to get shell access: docker exec -it <container_id> /bin/sh Or use docker attach for foreground containers.
results.title: Ensure sshd is not run within containers

results.details: No containers are publishing ports on all interfaces.
results.remediation: Bind published ports to a specific host IP instead of 0.0.0.0. Use -p 127.0.0.1:<host_port>:<container_port> for internal-only services. Remove EXPOSE directives from Dockerfiles for ports not required at runtime.
results.title: Ensure that only needed ports are open on the container

results.details: No containers are using --network=host.
results.remediation: Remove --network=host from docker run commands. Use Docker bridge or overlay networks and publish only the specific ports required with -p <host_port>:<container_port>.
results.title: Ensure that the host's network namespace is not shared

results.details: All containers have a memory limit configured.
results.remediation: Set a memory limit when starting containers: docker run --memory=<limit> (e.g. --memory=512m) Or set default memory limits in /etc/docker/daemon.json under "default-ulimits".
results.title: Ensure that the memory usage for containers is limited

results.details: All containers have explicit CPU shares configured.
results.remediation: Set CPU shares relative to other containers using: docker run --cpu-shares=<value> Default is 1024. Lower values get less CPU time under contention. Consider also --cpus= to set a hard CPU quota.
results.title: Ensure that CPU priority is set appropriately on containers

results.details: All containers have a read-only root filesystem.
results.remediation: Start containers with --read-only flag: docker run --read-only ... Mount writable paths explicitly as volumes: docker run --read-only -v /tmp:/tmp:rw ...
results.title: Ensure that the container's root filesystem is mounted as read only

results.details: All container port bindings are tied to a specific host interface.
results.remediation: Bind ports to a specific host IP: docker run -p 192.168.1.10:80:80 ...   # specific external NIC docker run -p 127.0.0.1:8080:80 ...    # localhost only Avoid -p 0.0.0.0:<port>:<port> or shorthand -p <port>:<port>.
results.title: Ensure that incoming container traffic is bound to a specific host interface

results.details: Containers without correct restart policy (on-failure, max 5): c7a07d962204f0cb5b6f89a3c6813757704c8c80434155e55634ef875b575ca3:RestartPolicy=unless-stopped MaxRetry=0
results.remediation: Set the restart policy when starting containers: docker run --restart=on-failure:5 ... For existing containers: docker update --restart=on-failure:5 <container_id>
results.title: Ensure that the on-failure container restart policy is set to 5

results.details: No containers are sharing the host PID namespace.
results.remediation: Remove --pid=host from docker run commands. Containers should use their own isolated PID namespace (the default).
results.title: Ensure that the host's process namespace is not shared

results.details: No containers are sharing the host IPC namespace.
results.remediation: Remove --ipc=host from docker run commands. If two containers need shared memory, use --ipc=container:<name> to share only between those containers, not with the host.
results.title: Ensure that the host's IPC namespace is not shared

results.details: No containers have host devices directly exposed.
results.remediation: Remove --device flags unless absolutely required. If a device is needed, restrict permissions to the minimum: docker run --device=/dev/snd:/dev/snd:r  (read-only) Never pass --device=/dev without a specific path.
results.title: Ensure that host devices are not directly exposed to containers

results.details: All containers have explicit ulimit overrides configured.
results.remediation: Set per-container ulimits at runtime: docker run --ulimit nofile=1024:1024 --ulimit nproc=100 ... Or configure daemon-wide defaults in /etc/docker/daemon.json: { "default-ulimits": { "nofile": { "Name": "nofile", "Hard": 64000, "Soft": 64000 } } }
results.title: Ensure that the default ulimit is overwritten at runtime if needed

results.details: No containers are using shared mount propagation.
results.remediation: Change mount propagation from shared to private or slave: docker run -v /host/path:/container/path:slave ... Remove :shared from any -v bind mount options.
results.title: Ensure mount propagation mode is not set to shared

results.details: No containers are sharing the host UTS namespace.
results.remediation: Remove --uts=host from docker run commands. Containers should use their own isolated UTS namespace (the default).
results.title: Ensure that the host's UTS namespace is not shared

results.details: All containers are using the default seccomp profile.
results.remediation: Remove --security-opt seccomp=unconfined from docker run commands. The Docker default seccomp profile blocks ~44 dangerous syscalls automatically. If a custom profile is needed: --security-opt seccomp=/path/to/profile.json
results.title: Ensure the default seccomp profile is not disabled

results.details: No docker exec --privileged usage found in daemon logs (last 7 days).
results.remediation: Never use: docker exec --privileged <container> <command> Use specific capabilities if elevated access is required in a running container. Audit all docker exec usage via centralized logging.
results.title: Ensure that docker exec commands are not used with the privileged option

results.details: No docker exec --user=root usage found in daemon logs (last 7 days).
results.remediation: Never use: docker exec --user=root <container> <command> Containers should run as a non-root user defined in the Dockerfile with USER directive. Use docker exec as that non-root user instead.
results.title: Ensure that docker exec commands are not used with the user=root option

results.details: All containers are using the default cgroup hierarchy.
results.remediation: Only use --cgroup-parent if required by your orchestrator. Confirm that custom cgroup parents still have resource limits enforced. Remove --cgroup-parent from containers where it was set unintentionally.
results.title: Ensure that cgroup usage is confirmed

results.details: Containers missing no-new-privileges: c7a07d962204f0cb5b6f89a3c6813757704c8c80434155e55634ef875b575ca3
results.remediation: Add --security-opt=no-new-privileges to all docker run commands. This prevents setuid/setgid programs from escalating privileges inside the container.
results.title: Ensure that the container is restricted from acquiring additional privileges

results.details: All containers have a health check configured.
results.remediation: Add a HEALTHCHECK instruction to your Dockerfile: HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --retries=3 CMD curl -f http://localhost/ || exit 1 Or pass at runtime: docker run --health-cmd="..." --health-interval=30s ...
results.title: Ensure that container health is checked at runtime

results.details: Containers using latest tag or untagged image: c7a07d962204f0cb5b6f89a3c6813757704c8c80434155e55634ef875b575ca3:Image=nginx:latest
results.remediation: Always pin images to a specific version tag or SHA digest: image: nginx:1.25.3   (version tag) image: nginx@sha256:abc123...  (digest — most secure) Avoid: image: nginx  or  image: nginx:latest
results.title: Ensure that Docker commands always make use of the latest version of their image

results.details: All containers have a PIDs cgroup limit configured.
results.remediation: Set a PID limit when starting containers: docker run --pids-limit=100 ... Choose a value appropriate to the expected workload. Even a high value (e.g. 1000) provides fork bomb protection.
results.title: Ensure that the PIDs cgroup limit is used

results.details: No containers are using the default docker0 bridge.
results.remediation: Create user-defined bridge networks and connect containers to them: docker network create my-app-network docker run --network=my-app-network ... This provides container DNS resolution and proper network isolation.
results.title: Ensure that Docker's default bridge docker0 is not used

results.details: No containers are sharing the host user namespace.
results.remediation: Remove --userns=host from docker run commands. Enable user namespace remapping in daemon.json for full UID isolation: { "userns-remap": "default" }
results.title: Ensure that the host's user namespaces are not shared

results.details: No containers have the Docker socket mounted.
results.remediation: Remove -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock from all docker run commands. If the container needs to manage Docker (e.g. CI agents), use the Docker TCP API with TLS authentication instead, or use purpose-built tools (Kaniko, Buildah) that do not require socket access.
results.title: Ensure that the Docker socket is not mounted inside any containers
